acme-sre: Hi team — over the last ~45m our calls to the hosted /v1/generate endpoint are returning a lot of 504s (and some 502s). Fail rate ~12%, p95 latency spiking. Our python SDK is retrying and we’re seeing a big unexpected token invoice. Request-id example: req-0a1b2c3d. Can you help triage?

maria_support: Sorry you hit this — we’re looking. Is this streaming or non-streaming generate? Any recent change to payloads or concurrency?

acme-sre: Non-streaming. No code change in past 24h. We ramped traffic from 200rps -> ~1.2k rps around 11:20UTC. Typical prompt ~1.5k tokens. Using official python SDK v0.8 with default retry/backoff.

josh_eng: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl or python) and one or two failing req IDs? Also which model name?

acme-sre: Sample python: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
for i in range(1000):
    resp = client.generate(model="rwd-large-1", prompt=my_prompt, max_tokens=512)
    print(resp.status_code)
```
Failing req IDs: req-0a1b2c3d, req-0d4e5f6a, req-0f7e8d9c

maria_support: thanks. Do you have `Authorization` header length or anything special (very long bearer, extra headers)? Also are you using connection pooling / keepalive?

acme-sre: Standard Bearer, keepalive:true via SDK default. No unusual headers.

sam_oncall: I see edge logs for tenant acme-123 around 11:20UTC where upstream returned 504 due to backend write stall. There are repeated client retries from same IP ranges which amplified queue pressure.

josh_eng: From runtime traces: GPU pool for rwd-large-1 in region-usw2 was at capacity and started dropping requests when prefix KV lock contention spiked (kvcache queue growth). Many requests had long prompts so each token cost was high. Looks like backpressure -> gateway timeouts.

maria_support: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Can we ask ACME to reduce concurrency / disable client retries for a short window? 2) We can enable tenant-side temporary concurrency cap to stop retry amplification. 3) Route them to a compatible smaller model variant while we sort runtime scaling.

acme-sre: We can lower concurrency from our side but it'd be better if you can throttle on your side while you investigate — reducing retries will reduce our billing impact.

devops-bot: Action: enabled tenant throttling for tenant acme-123 -> concurrency cap 50 (applied at 2098765980).

acme-sre: Thanks, I see fewer failures after ~11:26UTC. Billing still shows spike for the earlier window though. Any ETA on root cause?

josh_eng: Root cause hypothesis: sudden concurrent long-prompt burst exposed KV-cache lock contention in the serving runtime for this model variant. That created request queueing which then hit gateway timeouts; SDK retries amplified the traffic. We need to adjust batching/kvcache locks and add smarter per-tenant backpressure in runtime.

maria_support: For immediate customer guidance: 1) Set client-side max concurrency to 40 and enable exponential backoff with jitter. 2) Temporarily disable automatic retries in SDK (or set retries=1). 3) If acceptable, switch to `rwd-large-1-@lowlatency` variant (smaller context window) for the next 24h.

acme-sre: We switched to retries=1 and reduced worker concurrency. Failures dropped to ~0.5%. Please keep me posted on internal next steps.

josh_eng: Logged follow-up ticket INF-9248 for runtime KV cache lock improvements and a canary to route bursts to warm pools. Assigned to eng-runtime.

sam_oncall: Monitoring dashboards show error rate back to baseline after tenant cap + client changes. We'll keep throttling until eng confirms fix.

maria_support: FYI I'll open a billing reprieve request — asking finance to review the spike window for acme-123.

acme-sre: Really appreciate the fast help — thanks all. :pray:

maria_support: Marking this thread as triaged for now. Will update when INF-9248 has a patch or next steps. :eyes:
